newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI T-BILL REPO RATES END DOWN, SPOTS UP.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI T-BILL REPO RATES END DOWN, SPOTS UP.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday due to low fund demand from non-banking financial institutions during the slack summer season, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 9.02 percent from 10.70 percent on Thursday.

Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 3.94 million lots from 2.16 million lots with securities houses borrowing early-maturing contracts heavily to fund trading of new share issues, traders said.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

"The fund supply of non-banking financial institutions has increased recently due to low demand during the summer season," one trader said. "This made repo contracts trade at lower interest rates on Friday."

"Securities houses borrowed early-maturing contracts heavily today due to a number of new share issues in Shanghai and Shenzhen," said a second trader. "This pushed up volume today but was unable to support rates."
Traders said they believed repo rates would regain some lost ground early next week after falls on Thursday and Friday but trading would not be that active.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly higher on Friday on a technical rebound after a poor showing earlier this week, traders said.
The most actively traded seven-year bond that matures in August, 2003 rose to 100.00 yuan from 99.78 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose slightly to 654,439 lots on Friday from a thin 511,925 lots on Thursday.
Traders said light turnover indicated the market lacked liquidity and that the spot prices were likely to move narrowly in slow trading early next week.
